extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies, EPA staff, regulated power sector entities, and public commenters on EPA emissions rules
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and measurement/eligibility thresholds used in an EPA rulemaking establishing standards of performance and emissions guidelines for fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs). The page provides precise definitional criteria, measurement conventions, and regulatory references used to determine unit categories, outputs, and valid monitoring data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum electrical generating output (as-installed or uprated)
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum electrical generating output that a generator, prime mover, or other electric power production equipment under specific conditions designated by the manufacturer is capable of producing (in MWe, rounded to the nearest tenth) on a steady-state basis and during continuous operation (when not restricted by seasonal or other deratings) as of such installation as specified by the manufacturer of the equipment, or starting from the completion of any subsequent physical change resulting in an increase in the maximum electrical generating output ... such increased maximum amount (in MWe, rounded to the nearest tenth) as of such completion as specified by the person conducting the physical change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine unit capacity; measured in MWe rounded to nearest tenth; includes updated maximum after any physical change (uprate) as specified by manufacturer or reporting party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gas
rubrics_metrics.description: A fluid mixture of hydrocarbons (e.g., methane, ethane, or propane), composed of at least 70 percent methane by volume or that has a gross calorific value between 35 and 41 megajoules (MJ) per dry standard cubic meter (950 and 1,100 Btu per dry standard cubic foot), that maintains a gaseous state under ISO conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically excludes landfill gas, digester gas, refinery gas, sour gas, blast furnace gas, coal-derived gas, producer gas, coke oven gas, or any gaseous fuel produced in a process which might result in highly variable CO2 content or heating value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gas-fired steam generating unit
rubrics_metrics.description: An electric utility steam generating unit meeting the definition of 'fossil fuel-fired,' that is not a coal-fired or oil-fired steam generating unit, that no longer retains the capability to fire coal after December 31, 2029, and that burns natural gas for more than 10.0 percent of the average annual heat input during any continuous 3-calendar-year period after December 31, 2029, or for more than 15.0 percent of the annual heat input during any calendar year after December 31, 2029.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility/category determination based on heat input shares over specified post-2029 time windows (3-year rolling average >10% or single-year >15%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Net electric output
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of gross generation the generator(s) produce (including, but not limited to, output from steam turbine(s), combustion turbine(s), and gas expander(s)), as measured at the generator terminals, less the electricity used to operate the plant (i.e., auxiliary loads).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary loads include fuel handling equipment, pumps, fans, pollution control equipment, other electricity needs, and transformer losses as measured at the transmission side of the step up transformer (e.g., the point of sale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Net energy output
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined in two parts: (1) The net electric or mechanical output from the affected facility, plus 100 percent of the useful thermal output measured relative to standard ambient temperature and pressure conditions that is not used to generate additional electric or mechanical output or to enhance the performance of the unit. (2) For combined heat and power facilities meeting specified 12-month average thresholds (at least 20.0 percent electric/direct mechanical and at least 20.0 percent useful thermal), the net electric or mechanical output divided by 0.95, plus 100 percent of useful thermal output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful thermal output examples: steam delivered to an industrial process for heating. The 0.95 divisor applies only for CHP facilities meeting the 20%/20% thresholds on a 12-operating month rolling average.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oil-fired steam generating unit
rubrics_metrics.description: An electric utility steam generating unit meeting the definition of 'fossil fuel-fired' that is not a coal-fired steam generating unit, that no longer retains the capability to fire coal after December 31, 2029, and that burns oil for more than 10.0 percent of the average annual heat input during any continuous 3-calendar-year period after December 31, 2029, or for more than 15.0 percent of the annual heat input during any one calendar year after December 31, 2029.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category determination uses the same post-2029 percentage thresholds and time windows as the natural gas-fired steam generating unit definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard ambient temperature and pressure (SATP) conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: 298.15 Kelvin (25 °C, 77 °F) and 100.0 kilopascals (14.504 psi, 0.987 atm) pressure. The enthalpy of water at SATP conditions is 50 Btu/lb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference conditions for measuring useful thermal output and for energy/enthalpy calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: State agent
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity acting on behalf of the State, with the legal authority of the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify authorized actors for state-level implementation or submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stationary combustion turbine
rubrics_metrics.description: All equipment including, but not limited to, the turbine engine, the fuel, air, lubrication and exhaust gas systems, control systems (except emissions control equipment), heat recovery system, fuel compressor, heater, and/or pump, post-combustion emission control technology, and any ancillary components and sub-components comprising any simple cycle stationary combustion turbine, any combined cycle combustion turbine, and any combined heat and power combustion turbine based system plus any integrated equipment that provides electricity or useful thermal output to the combustion turbine engine, heat recovery system, or auxiliary equipment. Stationary means that the combustion turbine is not self-propelled or intended to be propelled while performing its function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be mounted on a vehicle for portability. A stationary combustion turbine that burns any solid fuel directly is considered a steam generating unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steam generating unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Any furnace, boiler, or other device used for combusting fuel and producing steam (nuclear steam generators are not included) plus any integrated equipment that provides electricity or useful thermal output to the affected facility or auxiliary equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines scope of devices considered steam generating units for applicability of standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: System Emergency
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods when the Reliability Coordinator has declared an Energy Emergency Alert level 2 or 3 as defined by NERC Reliability Standard EOP-011-2, or its successor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify exceptional grid conditions that may affect operations or compliance decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uprate
rubrics_metrics.description: An increase in available electric generating unit power capacity due to a system or equipment modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers use of updated maximum electrical generating output (see maximum output definition) for capacity/standards calculations after completion of physical changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Useful thermal output
rubrics_metrics.description: The thermal energy made available for use in any heating application (e.g., steam delivered to an industrial process for a heating application, including thermal cooling applications) that is not used for electric generation, mechanical output at the affected EGU, to directly enhance the performance of the affected EGU, or to supply energy to a pollution control device at the affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and measurement: economizer output is not useful thermal output, but thermal energy used to reduce fuel moisture is. For affected EGUs with no condensate return or where measuring condensate energy would not meaningfully impact emission rate calculation, useful thermal output is measured against SATP conditions. If there is meaningful condensate return (or other thermal input), the energy in the condensate must be measured and subtracted (relative to SATP) from measured thermal output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid data
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality-assured data generated by continuous monitoring systems that are installed, operated, and maintained according to 40 CFR part 75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CEMS: initial certification requirements in 40 CFR 75.20 and appendix A must be met before reporting; ongoing QA must meet daily, quarterly, and semiannual/annual test requirements in sections 2.1, 2.2, and 2.3 of appendix B and data validation criteria in sections 2.1.4, 2.2.3, and 2.3.2 of appendix B. For fuel flow meters: initial certification requirements in section 2.1.5 of appendix D to 40 CFR part 75 (except qualifying commercial billing meters under section 2.1.4.2) must be met before reporting; ongoing QA per provisions in section 2.1.6 of appendix D (with noted exceptions for qualifying commercial billing meters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waste-to-Energy
rubrics_metrics.description: A process or unit (e.g., solid waste incineration unit) that recovers energy from the conversion or combustion of waste stream materials, such as municipal solid waste, to generate electricity and/or heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies waste-combustion processes that produce useful energy and may be treated under specific program definitions.
